headerDisplay:
Shows a Texecom **Premier Elite** alarm in the Apple Home app: an alarm you can arm and disarm, and a sensor for each zone.

**You'll need** the panel's **UDL code**, and either a Texecom **SmartCom or ComIP** on your network, a serial-to-network adapter, or a serial cable to the panel. Work down the page: 1, 2, 3. Section 4 can be left as it is.
footerDisplay: Arming from the Home app works for areas 1-8. With Crestron, after an arm or disarm from the Home app the panel holds back its other messages for about 30 seconds, so sensor changes in that time show late.

name.title: Name in the Homebridge log
name.description: Only used in the Homebridge log. You don't need to change it.

protocol.title: How does Homebridge reach your panel?

oneOf.title: Crestron (a COM port set to Crestron System)
Texecom Connect (SmartCom or ComIP as normal)

protocol.description: Not sure? If you have a SmartCom (the box the Texecom app uses), Texecom Connect is the easiest: nothing on the panel needs changing and your zones are found automatically. While Homebridge is connected the Texecom app can't use the SmartCom. Choose Crestron if one of the panel's COM ports is set to "Crestron System" (your installer, or Wintex, can set this): through a ComIP, a serial-to-network adapter or a serial cable.

ip_address.title: IP address of the SmartCom, ComIP or adapter
ip_address.description: Find it in your router's list of connected devices, and reserve it there so it doesn't change. Leave blank only if you use a serial cable.

ip_port.title: Port
ip_port.description: SmartCom or ComIP: 10001. A serial-to-network adapter (for example an ESP8266 running ser2net): the port set on the adapter, often 23.

serial_device.title: Serial port (serial cable only)
serial_device.description: Only if the panel is wired to this machine with a USB-serial cable. Leave blank when you've entered an IP address.

baud_rate.title: Serial speed
baud_rate.description: Must match the panel's COM port. Leave at 19200 unless your installer changed it.

udl.title: UDL code
udl.description: The panel's remote-access code, used by Texecom's Wintex software. It isn't a keypad user code. Texecom panels come with 1234, and most keep it; if that doesn't work, your installer may have changed it. Needed to arm and disarm from the Home app, and always needed for Texecom Connect.

dwell.title: Hold time (ms)
dwell.description: Keeps the sensor showing "detected" for this long after the zone clears, so short movements still trigger automations. 0 = off; 5000 = 5 seconds.

area_number.title: Area number
area_number.description: 1 for area A on the keypad, 2 for area B, and so on. Areas 1-8 can be armed from the Home app.

zones.title: Zones in this area
zones.description: Only needed with "Raise an alarm from zone activity" under Advanced.

homekit_modes.title: Buttons to show in the Home app (Off is always shown)
homekit_modes.description: Tick only the modes you use. Nothing ticked = all three. Most homes use Away and Night. If you change this later, the alarm reappears in the Home app as a new accessory (the Home app remembers the old buttons), so you'll need to set its room and automations again.

night_part_arm.title: Night arms
night_part_arm.description: Your panel's part arms are set up by your installer, each covering a chosen set of zones (for example, downstairs only). Blank = Part Arm 1. Area 1 only.

home_part_arm.title: Home arms
home_part_arm.description: Blank = Part Arm 1, the same as Night. If Home would do the same as Night, untick Home above instead.

part_arm_3.title: Part Arm 3 is
part_arm_3.description: Texecom Connect reports exactly which part arm is set. Choose the Home app mode for each; Night and Home arm the first part arm set to that mode.

default_arm_state.title: Arms from the keypad or a keyfob show as
default_arm_state.description: With Crestron the panel reports "armed" without saying whether it was a full or part arm. Arms made from the Home app always show the mode you chose. Away suits most homes.

remote_users.title: Keyfob users (always shown as Away)
remote_users.description: Panel user numbers of keyfobs or remotes. Leave empty if you don't use them.

status_poll_interval.title: Check the panel every (seconds)
status_poll_interval.description: Asks the panel which areas are armed, which corrects the Home app if a message was missed and reconnects if the panel stops answering. Recommended: 60. 0 = off.

time_sync_interval.title: Keep the panel clock right (hours between checks)
time_sync_interval.description: Compares the panel clock with your local time and corrects it if it's more than a minute out, for example after a power cut. 24 is a good choice, with your time zone set below. 0 = off.

time_zone.title: Your time zone
time_zone.description: Used by the clock check, so the panel shows your local time. Homebridge in Docker usually runs on UTC, so set this (e.g. Europe/London) whenever the clock check is on. Without it, the clock check won't move the panel's clock by whole hours.

trigger_from_zones.title: Raise an alarm from zone activity
trigger_from_zones.description: Leave off. The panel reports real alarms itself; this guesses from movement instead, and goes off every time someone uses the normal way in while the entry timer runs. Only for panels that don't report alarms.

debug.title: Detailed logging
debug.description: Logs every message from the panel. Useful when reporting a problem; leave off otherwise.

layout.title: 2. Zones and areas
layout.description:
A zone is one detector or door contact; each appears in the Home app as a sensor you can use in automations. An area is a part of the system armed on its own; each appears as an alarm with arm buttons. Most homes have one area. Zone and area numbers are the ones on your keypad and in Wintex.
Texecom Connect: nothing to fill in here. Zones and areas, with their names, are read from the panel.

layout.title: 3. Arm modes in the Home app
layout.description: The Home app's alarm has an Off button and up to three arm buttons. Away fully arms the panel. Night and Home set one of the panel's part arms (each part arm covers a set of zones your installer chose).

layout.title: 4. Advanced (can be left as they are)
